title: 🛡️ OpenAI and Cisco Launch "Sherwood"… Temporary Shields That Protect Linux Without Stopping the Service!
body: 🛡️ OpenAI and Cisco Launch "Sherwood"… Temporary Shields That Protect Linux Without Stopping the Service!
OpenAI and Cisco have launched a new project called "Sherwood", aimed at protecting Linux systems from attacks without needing to stop services.

The idea is based on temporary protection measures known as "shields", installed quickly to close a vulnerability while the permanent fix is being prepared, so the system is not left exposed during the wait.

"Sherwood" works with eBPF technology, which makes it possible to intercept exploitation attempts and block them, without disrupting the system's normal activity or stopping the services users rely on.

The project also supports AI agents that can scan for security vulnerabilities, develop protection measures, and test them before deployment, in a step that makes AI a partner in defense, not just a tool for attack.

The two companies demonstrated the idea in practice: the "Codex" model used a shield to block the exploitation of a "Log4Shell" vulnerability targeting a search service running at the time of the demo, stopping the attack without the service going down.
Simply put: a temporary shield protects your system until the permanent fix arrives; would you prefer a quick temporary protection or waiting for the full fix?
Would you trust an AI agent to write protection for your system by itself?
